title: Write a cron file with a copy of bash named dpkg
threat_model: An attacker names the writing program after a package manager, which is allowed to write there, so that a name-based allow list ignores it.
known_gap: persistence skips writers whose comm is on its expected-writer list, and the comm is the name of the file that was run, so a copy named dpkg is suppressed.
notes: setup.sh copies /bin/bash to a file named dpkg in the work directory. The action runs it by that path and it writes a comment line to the cron file. The real dpkg is not run.
